findings.title: Breaking change: recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes the old value 4. This is a behavior change for any user/automation that relies on the previous exit code 4 to detect a recreate upgrade. The previous docs (update-compatibility.adoc) already listed 3 as the recreate code, so this PR brings the code in line with the documented contract, but it is still a silent behavior change for existing callers that depended on the buggy value. Consider calling this out in release notes or, since the tool is preview, leave the old code path with a deprecation alias.

findings.title: Tests assert error messages but never assert exit codes
findings.body: testCompatible only asserts `assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())` for the OK case, while testWrongVersions and the new testFeatureNotEnabled only assert on the printed error/message text, never on the numeric exit code. This is exactly the gap that allowed the previous `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4` bug to exist while the docs claimed exit code 3. Without exit-code assertions, a future regression that swaps 3 and 4 (or assigns the wrong constant) will not be caught. Add `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, result.exitCode())` (and the corresponding FEATURE_DISABLED assertion) so the contract is enforced.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand
findings.body: The new feature-gate branch was added to both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), but testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The check subcommand has identical feature-flag logic and is left untested for the disabled case, so a future regression that, for example, removes the guard from one of the two run() methods will go unnoticed. Add a symmetric test for `UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME` that asserts both the 'feature disabled' error and exit code 4.

findings.title: Error message references generic 'this command' instead of the actual command
findings.body: printFeatureDisabled() emits "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." Both subcommands have a clearer name (update-compatibility check / metadata) and the message will be displayed to operators running the CLI. The generic wording also doesn't match the more specific phrasing used in the docs (`docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc` says "the commands will fail"). Consider naming the command or, at minimum, matching the doc wording so the user immediately knows which command failed.
